description: Chives are a perennial herb in the Allium genus related to garlic, shallots, leeks, scallions, and Chinese onions. They are grown for culinary and ornamental purposes. The scapes or stems are hollow and tubular and have a mild onion taste. They are one of the fines herbes of French cuisine and commonly used fresh. The plant forms dense clusters of slender 2-3cm bulbs, which can be cooked. Chive flowers are edible, star-shaped, and pale purple. Chives are a good companion plant because their sulfur compounds repel negative insects, and their flowers attract bees.
sowing_method: Direct seed. If planting indoors, harden off before transplanting seedlings outside.

growing_information.text: This is a small onion-like plant having flat, hollow leaves which are used for flavoring soups. The chive rarely forms seeds, and it is propagated by the bulbs, which grow in clusters. The leaves may be cut freely and are soon replaced by others.—(F. B. 255; S. Dak. E. S. 68.)

growing_information.text:
Chives are perfectly hardy perennial little members of the onion tribe, and are grown exclusively for their tops, which are used wherever the flavor of onion is required. Planted in small clumps in any common garden soil, they will grow readily, and in time increase so as to render a division necessary. The tops appear very early in spring, and can be shorn throughout the season, hence this valuable little plant should have a place in every garden.

growing_information.text: Chives are hardy perennial plants belonging to the onion family, valued for their flavorful leaves used in various dishes. They are best propagated by dividing clumps of bulbs, as they rarely produce seeds. Plant chive bulbs 7-10cm (three or four inches) deep and 30cm (12in) apart in rows that are spaced 60cm (2ft) apart. Chives thrive in well-drained soil and can be grown in any common garden soil, making them suitable for most gardens. They are best planted in early spring, but can also be planted in autumn if the weather is mild. The leaves emerge very early in spring and can be harvested throughout the growing season. Regular harvesting encourages new growth. Chives are relatively pest-free, but keep an eye out for common onion pests such as thrips and onion maggots. To maintain a healthy patch, divide the clumps every three to four years or when they become overcrowded.
